{{URL|http://www.marutisuzuki.com/}} | area_served = India }} '''Maruti Suzuki India Limited''' is the Indian [[subsidiary]] of Japanese automaker [[Suzuki|Suzuki Motor Corporation]]. It is the largest automobile manufacturer in India, specializing in [[Subcompact car|small cars]]. As of 2025, the company had a market capitalization of approximately US$50-55 billion.{{cite web|url=https://money.usnews.com/investing/articles/the-10-most-valuable-auto-companies-in-the-world|title=The 10 Most Valuable Auto Companies in the World|website=Money.usnews.com|access-date=13 July 2026}} The company was established by the [[Government of India]] as Maruti Udyog Limited in February 1981 as a joint venture with Suzuki, the latter becoming the first Japanese automaker, as well as the first major foreign automaker, to invest in India.{{cite news|url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/obituary-osamu-suzuki-who-led-japanese-automaker-into-india-dies-94-2024-12-27/|title=Osamu Suzuki, who led Japanese automaker into India, dies at 94|first=Chang-Ran|last=Kim|publisher=Reuters|date=December 27, 2024|access-date=December 27, 2024}}{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2024/12/27/business/osamu-suzuki-dies-94.html|title=Osamu Suzuki, Who Led Japanese Carmaker for Over 4 Decades, Dies at 94|first1=River Akira|last1=Davis|first2=Kiuko|last2=Notoya|work=New York Times|date=27 December 2024|access-date=27 December 2024}}{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/industry/auto/auto-news/osamu-suzuki-the-legend-who-was-instrumental-in-helping-india-kickstart-its-automotive-journey/articleshow/116709084.cms?from=mdr|title=Osamu Suzuki: The legend who was instrumental in helping India kickstart its automotive journey|publisher=The Economic Times|date=27 December 2024}} Maruti opened its first production facility in [[Gurgaon|Gurugram, Haryana]], in 1982.{{Cite web |date=2021-08-27 |title=Maruti Suzuki Case Study - History and Success in India |url=https://startuptalky.com/maruti-suzuki-case-study-india/ |access-date=2023-04-07 |website=StartupTalky |language=en}} Initially, Maruti was majority-owned by the Indian government, with Suzuki only taking a 26% stake during its establishment in 1982. The Indian government gradually reduced its stake, partially departed the business in 2003 by making it a public company and then sold all of its remaining shares to Suzuki Motor Corporation in 2007.[http://marutisuzuki.com/corporate.aspx Maruti Suzuki Corporate Information] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130126163908/http://marutisuzuki.com/corporate.aspx|date=26 January 2013}}. Retrieved 2013-02-01.{{Cite news |date=2007-05-10 |title=Govt exits Maruti, sells residual stake for 2,360 cr |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/govt-exits-maruti-sells-residual-stake-for-2360-cr/articleshow/2027888.cms |access-date=2023-04-07 |issn=0971-8257}} Maruti Suzuki has emerged as the largest Suzuki subsidiary in terms of production volume and sales. As of September 2022, the company had a leading market share of 42% in the [[Automotive industry in India|Indian passenger car market]].{{Cite web |date=21 November 2022 |title=Maruti Suzuki chases market share but losing 'mind share' to Tata Motors |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/news/business/markets/maruti-suzuki-chases-market-share-but-losing-mind-share-to-tata-motors-9572511.html |access-date=2022-12-14 |website=Moneycontrol |language=en}} == History == === Pre-Suzuki affiliation === The Maruti name can be traced back to a previous company that was established by the third Indian Prime Minister [[Indira Gandhi]]'s son, [[Sanjay Gandhi]]. In the early 1970s, the Indian government initiated the search for a small car manufacturer. At that time, India had already been manufacturing cars for several years, and the idea of a more affordable "people's car" had been discussed since the 1950s. Sanjay Gandhi, known for his passion for cars, apprenticed with [[Rolls-Royce]] in [[Crewe]] of UK for three years. Upon his return in 1968, he recognized the potential of small car production in the private sector. Both the government and the [[Planning Commission (India)|Planning Commission]] endorsed the concept. Sanjay Gandhi subsequently initiated his automotive project, establishing operations in a rented garage near [[Roshanara Bagh]] in [[Old Delhi]]. The government issued a [[letter of intent]] in September 1970, with plan to produce up to 50,000 cars in a year. In August 1971, '''Maruti Motors Limited''' was established with [[Sanjay Gandhi]] becoming its first [[managing director]]. He acquired 297 acres of land in [[Gurgaon]] at a cost of approximately Rs 12,000 per acre to establish his Maruti factory.{{Cite web |date=2015-04-14 |title=Maruti and Sanjay Gandhi: The history of an illicit, extraordinary love affair |url=https://www.motoroids.com/features/maruti-and-sanjay-gandhi-the-history-of-an-illicit-extraordinary-love-affair/ |access-date=2024-04-12 |website=Motoroids |language=en-GB}} Initially, plans were laid out to manufacture an indigenous car priced at around Rs 8,000. However, the cost of the vehicle escalated to approximately Rs 16,500 (ex-showroom) and about Rs 21,000 on the road in Haryana. Despite the increase in price, the Maruti car remained competitively priced, being Rs 5,000-10,000 cheaper than its counterparts. The first prototype of the Maruti car was completed in 1972, with production anticipated to commence by April 1973, as promised by Sanjay Gandhi.{{Cite book |last=Sen |first=Gautam |title=A million cars for a billion people: the story of India's 'millionaire' cars, - from the iconic Maruti 800 to what went horribly wrong with the Tata Nano |date=2014 |publisher=Platinum Press |isbn=978-93-84027-74-2 |location=Mumbai, India}} He made the [[chassis]] by himself at his workshop, and a [[Triumph Motorcycles Ltd|Triumph]] motorcycle engine was used to propel the car. the prototype car underwent a feasibility test by the Vehicle Research & Development Establishment in [[Ahmednagar]]. The prototype failed the test, being deemed unsuitable for road use. Nonetheless, in July 1974, Maruti was granted an industrial license to produce 50,000 cars.{{Cite web |last=Bhandari |first=Bhupesh |date=2015-07-11 |title=Emergency and Sanjay Gandhi: How Maruti's origin lies in cronyism, corruption and blackmail |url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/beyond-business/emergency-and-the-maruti-story-start-of-a-small-wonder-115070900758_1.html}} However, the actual production output at Sanjay Gandhi's factory fell short of the initial target. Despite the projection to commence production at a rate of 12-20 units per month and escalate to 200 units per day, only 21 units were manufactured by 31 March 1976.{{Cite news |date=2023-12-14 |title=Was Maruti 800 truly the brainchild of Sanjay Gandhi? |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/new-updates/was-maruti-800-truly-the-brainchild-of-sanjay-gandhi/articleshow/105978938.cms?from=mdr |access-date=2024-04-12 |work=The Economic Times |issn=0013-0389}} Sanjay Gandhi's involvement in politics during [[The Emergency (India)|the Emergency]] further complicated the project's progress. Following Indira Gandhi's defeat in the 1977 election and a [[court order]] for Maruti's dissolution in 1978, the project faced uncertain prospects. With Indira's return to office in 1980 and Sanjay's death in a plane crash, the Government of India intervened and assumed control of Maruti through [[legislative]] measures. === Tie-up with Suzuki === [[File:Maruti Old Logo.JPG|thumb|Logo of Maruti Udyog]] Following Sanjay's death, his mother Indira tasked [[Arun Nehru]] with evaluating the feasibility of resurrecting her son's vision to develop India's affordable car. Nehru acknowledged the project's potential but emphasized the need for expertise from an experienced manufacturer. Subsequently, a team was assembled to explore potential collaborations with manufacturers globally. The Indian government started engaging in negotiations with [[Suzuki]] in April 1982. Following several months of preparations, Suzuki of Japan and '''Maruti Udyog Ltd.''' signed a license and [[joint venture]] agreement in October 1982. Initially, Suzuki acquired a modest 26 percent stake in the joint venture, owing to their constrained capital and perceived risks, despite the Indian government's preference for Suzuki to take a 40 percent [[Foreign direct investment|foreign equity share]]. Both parties reached a consensus, stipulating that Suzuki would increase its stake to 40 percent after five years.{{Cite web |last=Sorabjee |first=Hormazd |date=2023-12-15 |title=No one knew what Maruti 800's launch would lead to: RC Bhargava |url=https://www.autocarindia.com/auto-features/no-one-knew-what-maruti-800s-launch-would-lead-to-rc-bhargava-430104 |access-date=2024-04-12 |website=Autocar India}} Both the venture partners also entered into an agreement to nominate their candidate for the post of managing director and every managing director would have a tenure of five years."[http://www.rediff.com/business/sep/19maru.htm Rediff on the Net: A successful marriage goes to court]", 19 September 1997{{cite web |date=3 September 1997 |title=Rediff |url=http://www.rediff.com/business/sep/03mul.htm |access-date=10 October 2010 |work=Rediff.com}} Suzuki later increased its equity to 50% in 1992, and further to 56.21% as of 2013.{{Cite web |date=2013-04-01 |title=The Times of India |url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/Suzuki-Motors-stake-in-Maruti-Suzuki-goes-up-to-56-21/articleshow/19323285.cms |website=[[The Times of India]]}} Maruti was granted permission to import two Suzuki vehicles that were completely assembled in the first two years of India's closed market, with an initial target of using just 33% domestic components. This greatly displeased the nearby manufacturers. There were some concerns that the Indian market would not support Maruti Suzuki's relatively high production levels, and the government even considered changing the petrol tariff and decreasing the excise fee to increase sales.{{cite journal |author=B M |date=2021-08-30 |title=Message of Maruti-Suzuki |journal=Economic and Political Weekly |location=Mumbai, India |publisher=Sameeksha Trust |volume=XVII |pages=1524–1525 |number=38}} [[File:Suzuki Maruti 800 1996 (14855426712).jpg|thumb|A 1996 [[Maruti 800]] photographed in Chile]] Local production commenced in December 1983 with the introduction of the [[Suzuki Fronte#SS30/SS40|SS30/SS40 Suzuki Fronte/Alto]]-based [[Maruti 800]].{{cite web |title=Maruti's domestic sales crosses 1 cr mark |url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/maruti-suzuki-sales-cross-1-cr-mark/909976/ |access-date=9 February 2021 |work=[[The Indian Express]]}} In 1984, the [[Suzuki Carry|Maruti Van]] with the same three-cylinder engine as the 800 was released. Maruti targeted annual production of 20,000 cars in the first year, and 40,000 in the second year at the [[Gurgaon]] plant. However, the rapid success of Maruti exceeded expectations of Suzuki. Within the first year, the company received an 120,000 bookings, much to Suzuki's surprise. Despite facing overwhelming demand, Maruti encountered challenges in meeting orders due to capacity limitations. The surge in demand necessitated a complete overhaul of its production strategy, by adjusting the ratio between the 800 and the van. The [[Maruti Suzuki Gypsy|Suzuki SJ410-based Gypsy]], a 970 cc 4-wheel drive off-road vehicle, was introduced in 1985. The 100,000th car manufactured by the firm was the 796 cc hatchback [[Suzuki Alto|Suzuki Alto (SS80)]], which succeeded the original 800 in 1986.{{Cite web |title=The Maruti Udyog official Website Timeline Page |url=http://www.marutiudyog.com/ab/aboutus.asp?ch=1&ct=1&sc=6 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071012122151/http://www.marutiudyog.com/ab/aboutus.asp?ch=1&ct=1&sc=6 |archive-date=12 October 2007}} In 1987, the company started exporting to western markets, when a lot of 500 cars were sent to Hungary. By 1988, the capacity of the Gurgaon plant was increased to 100,000 units per annum. Until 1992–1993, Maruti faced constraints in increasing capacity due to the need for [[foreign exchange]]. Moreover, securing funding for expansion was challenging, especially during the [[1991 Indian economic crisis|Indian economic crisis of 1991]]. The Indian government stipulated that expansion could only proceed with foreign loans to cover costs. Eventually, Maruti secured aid from Axiom Bank in Japan, allowing them to finance the [[foreign exchange]] component of their expansion. This enabled Maruti to establish a new production line in the Gurgaon plant, addressing the persistent issue of shortages. In 1989, the [[Maruti 1000]] was introduced and the 970 cc, [[Three-box styling|three-box]] was India's first contemporary [[sedan (car)|sedan]]. By 1991, 65 percent of the components, for all vehicles produced, were indigenized. After the liberalization of the [[Economy of India|Indian economy]] in 1991, Suzuki increased its stake in Maruti to 50 percent, making the company a 50-50 joint venture with the government of India as the other stakeholder. In 1993, the [[Maruti Suzuki Zen|Zen]], a 993 cc engine hatchback was launched, and in 1994 the 1,298 cc [[Suzuki Cultus Crescent|Esteem]] sedan was introduced. Maruti produced its 1 millionth vehicle since the commencement of production in 1994. Maruti's second plant was opened with an annual capacity reaching 200,000 units. Maruti launched a 24-hour emergency on-road vehicle service. In 1998, the new Maruti 800 was released, being the first change in design since 1986. Zen D, a 1,527 cc diesel hatchback, Maruti's first diesel vehicle, and a redesigned Omni were introduced. In 1999, the 1.6-litre [[Maruti Baleno]] three-box sedan and [[Suzuki Wagon R|Wagon R]] were also launched. In 2000, Maruti became the first car company in India to launch a [[Call Center|call center]] for internal and customer services. The new [[Maruti Suzuki Alto|Alto]] model was released. In 2001, [[#Maruti TrueValue|Maruti True Value]], selling and buying used cars was launched. In October of the same year, the [[Suzuki Carry|Maruti Versa]] was launched. In 2002, [[Suzuki Cultus Crescent|Esteem]] Diesel was introduced. Two new subsidiaries were also started: Maruti Insurance Distributor Services and Maruti Insurance Brokers Limited. Suzuki Motor Corporation increased its stake in Maruti to 54.2 percent. In 2003, the new [[Suzuki Vitara|Suzuki Grand Vitara]] XL-7 was introduced while the [[Maruti Suzuki Zen|Zen]] and the [[Suzuki Wagon R|Wagon R]] were upgraded and redesigned. The four millionth Maruti vehicle was built and they entered into a partnership with the [[State Bank of India]]. Maruti Udyog Ltd. was listed on BSE and NSE after a public issue, which was oversubscribed tenfold. In 2004, the [[Maruti Suzuki Alto|Alto]] became India's best-selling car overtaking the [[Maruti 800]] after nearly two decades. The five-seater [[Suzuki Carry|Versa]] 5-seater, a new variant, was created while the Esteem was re-launched. Maruti Udyog closed the financial year 2003–04 with an annual sale of 472,122 units, the highest ever since the company began operations, and the fiftieth lakh (5 millionth) car rolled out in April 2005. The 1.3-litre [[Suzuki Swift]] five-door hatchback was introduced in 2005.{{cite journal | title = Maruti Udyog: Smooth Drive | journal = Economic and Political Weekly | number = 8 | volume = XLI | location = Mumbai, India | publisher = Sameeksha Trust | page = 672 | date = 2006-02-25 }} [[File:Maruti Suzuki logo (2009).svg|thumb|Maruti Suzuki's former logo, used in 2009-2018]] In 2006, Suzuki and Maruti set up another joint venture called Maruti Suzuki Automobiles India to build two new manufacturing plants, one for vehicles and one for engines. Cleaner cars were also introduced, with several new models meeting the new [[Bharat Stage emission standards|Bharat Stage III emission standards]]. In February 2012, Maruti Suzuki sold its ten millionth vehicle in India. In July 2014 it had a market share of more than 45%.{{Cite web|url=http://www.team-bhp.com/forum/indian-car-scene/154170-july-2014-indian-car-sales-figures-analysis.html|title=July 2014: Indian Car Sales Figures & Analysis - Team-BHP|access-date=2016-06-28}} In May 2015, the company produced its fifteen millionth vehicle in India, a Swift Dzire.{{cite web|title=Maruti Suzuki rolls out 15 million cars {{!}} Team-BHP|url=http://www.team-bhp.com/news/maruti-suzukis-manesar-plant-rolls-out-15-million-cars|access-date=10 May 2020|website=Team-BHP.com|language=en}} On 25 April 2019, Maruti Suzuki announced that it would phase out production of [[Diesel engine|diesel cars]] by 1 April 2020, when the [[Bharat Stage emission standards|Bharat Stage VI emission standards]] come into effect. The new standards would require a significant investment from the company to upgrade its existing diesel engines to comply with the more stringent emission standards. Chairman [[R. C. Bhargava|R.C. Bhargava]] stated, "We have taken this decision so that in 2022 we are able to meet the corporate average fuel efficiency (CAFE) norms and a higher share of [[Compressed natural gas|CNG]] vehicles will help us comply with the norms. I hope the union government's policies will help grow the market for CNG vehicles." At that time, diesel cars accounted for about 23 percent of Maruti Suzuki's annual sales.{{cite web |last1=Ghosh |first1=Malyaban |title=Maruti to phase out all diesel cars from April next year |url=https://www.livemint.com/auto-news/maruti-to-phase-out-all-diesel-cars-from-april-next-year-1556184892655.html |website=Mint |access-date=26 April 2019 |language=en |date=25 April 2019}} The company planned to launch its first [[electric car]] in the second half of 2021, the Maruti Suzuki Wagon R Electric, before cancelling its plan.{{Cite web|title=Maruti Suzuki WagonR electric test mule spotted yet again|url=https://www.timesnownews.com/auto/car-news/article/maruti-suzuki-wagonr-electric-test-mule-spotted-yet-again/774784|access-date=2021-06-25|website=Timesnownews.com|date=23 June 2021 |language=en}} The company now produces the eVitara (unveiled in Milan and based on eVX concept shown in 2023) since 2025.{{Cite web|title=Maruti Suzuki e Vitara unveiled: All about company's first-ever electric vehicle, set for 2025 production|url=https://www.livemint.com/auto-news/maruti-suzuki-e-vitara-unveiled-all-about-companys-first-ever-electric-vehicle-set-for-2025-production/-11730811769761.html|access-date=2024-11-12|website=live mint|date=2024-11-05 |language=en}} == Leadership == * [[Sanjay Gandhi]] (1971–1977) * [[R. C. Bhargava]] (1981–1997) * S. S. L. N. Bhaskarudu (1997–1999) * [[Jagdish Khattar]] (1999–2007){{cite web | url=https://www.afaqs.com/news/marketing/19527_Khattar-retires-from-Maruti-Suzuki-top-management-reshuffled | title=Khattar retires from Maruti Suzuki; top management reshuffled | website=Afaqs.com | date=30 October 2007 | access-date=3 September 2020 }} * Shinzo Nakanishi (2007–2013){{cite web | title=Maruti Suzuki India makes changes in top management; Jagdish Khattar to retire in December - Exchange4media | date=30 October 2007 | url=https://www.exchange4media.com/people-movement-news/maruti-suzuki-india-makes-changes-in-top-managementjagdish-khattar-to-retire-in-december-28385.html }} * Kenichi Ayukawa (2013–2022){{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2013-03-15/maruti-suzuki-names-ayukawa-ceo-amid-indian-car-market-slump#:~:text=Gift%20this%20article,March%202003%2C%20the%20group%20said|title=Maruti Suzuki Names Ayukawa CEO Amid Indian Car Market Slump|website=Bloomberg.com|access-date=July 13, 2026}} * Hisashi Takeuchi (2022–present){{cite web | title=Maruti Suzuki Board Appoints Mr Hisashi Takeuchi as MD & CEO starting 1st April '22 | url=https://www.marutisuzuki.com/corporate/media/press-releases/2022/march/maruti-suzuki-board-appoints-mr-hisashi-takeuchi-as-md-and-ceo-starting-1st-april-22#:~:text=Maruti%20Suzuki%20is%20a%20great,By%20Year }} ==Manufacturing facilities== Maruti Suzuki has two manufacturing facilities in [[Haryana]] ([[Gurgaon|Gurugram]] and [[Manesar]]), and [[Suzuki Motor Gujarat|one manufacturing complex in Gujarat]]. All manufacturing facilities have a combined production capacity of 2,250,000 vehicles annually. The [[Gurgaon|Gurugram]] manufacturing facility has three fully integrated manufacturing plants and is spread over {{convert|300|acre|km2}}.{{Cite web|url=https://www.businesstoday.in/magazine/cover-story/maruti-suzuki-on-recovery-route-after-2012-labour-troubles/story/202165.html|title=How Maruti bounced back after its labour strife of 2012|website=Businesstoday.in|date=15 January 2014 }} The Gurugram facilities also manufacture 240,000 ''[[List of Suzuki engines#K engine|K-Series]]'' engines annually. The Gurugram facility manufactures the [[Suzuki Alto|Alto 800]], [[Maruti Suzuki Wagon R|Wagon R]], [[Suzuki Ertiga|Ertiga]], XL6, [[Suzuki SX4|S-Cross]], [[Suzuki Brezza|Vitara Brezza]], [[Suzuki Ignis|Ignis]], and [[Suzuki Eeco|Eeco]]. The Gurugram facility also assembles the [[Suzuki Jimny|Jimny]] starting from January 2021 solely for export markets. It was reported the Indian-assembled Jimny will be exported to African markets and countries in the Middle East.{{Cite web|title=Maruti Suzuki starts exporting the Jimny SUV from India|url=https://www.autocarindia.com/car-news/maruti-suzuki-starts-exporting-the-jimny-suv-from-india-419712|access-date=2021-01-20|website=Autocar India|language=en}} The [[Manesar]] manufacturing plant was inaugurated in February 2007 and is spread over {{convert|600|acre|km2}}. Initially, it had a production capacity of 100,000 vehicles annually but this was increased to 300,000 vehicles annually in October 2008. The production capacity was further increased by 250,000 vehicles taking the total production capacity to 800,000 vehicles annually.{{Cite web |url=http://www.marutisuzuki.com/press-release-16-sep-2014.aspx |title=Maruti Suzuki India LTD. Maruti Udyog Ltd Best Selling Car Maruti True Value Maruti Udyog |access-date=24 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150225025355/http://www.marutisuzuki.com/press-release-16-sep-2014.aspx |archive-date=25 February 2015 |url-status=dead }} The Manesar plant produces the [[Maruti Suzuki Alto|Alto]], [[Suzuki Swift|Swift]], [[Suzuki Ciaz|Ciaz]], [[Suzuki Baleno (2015)|Baleno]] and [[Suzuki Celerio|Celerio]]. On 25 June 2012, Haryana State Industries and Infrastructure Development Corporation demanded Maruti Suzuki pay an additional ₹235 crore for enhanced land acquisition for its Haryana plant expansion. The agency reminded Maruti that failure to pay the amount would lead to further proceedings and vacating the enhanced land acquisition.{{cite news|title=Haryana government asks Maruti to pay Rs 235 crore for farmer compensation|work=The Economic Times|date=24 July 2012|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics/nation/haryana-government-asks-maruti-to-pay-rs-235-crore-for-farmer-compensation/articleshow/15123404.cms}} In 2012, the company decided to merge Suzuki Powertrain India Limited (SPIL) with itself.{{Cite web|title=Maruti to merge Suzuki Powertrain with itself; Suzuki to increase stake to 56.21%|url=http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-06-13/news/32215543_1_diesel-engine-powertrain-india-maruti-suzuki|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150602045356/http://articles.economictimes.indiatimes.com/2012-06-13/news/32215543_1_diesel-engine-powertrain-india-maruti-suzuki|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 June 2015|access-date=2016-07-13}} SPIL was started as a JV by Suzuki Motor Corp. along with Maruti Suzuki. It has the facilities available for manufacturing diesel engines and transmissions. The demand for transmissions for all Maruti Suzuki cars is met by the production from SPIL. In 2017, the new [[Suzuki Motor Gujarat]] facility was opened. This third facility is not owned by Maruti Suzuki, but instead wholly owned by Suzuki Motor Corporation. Despite that, the plant supplied vehicles to Maruti without any additional cost. Located in Hansalpur, [[Ahmedabad]], the plant has a total annual capacity of 750,000 units. In November 2021 Maruti Suzuki announce to set up of a big plant in [[Kharkhoda, Haryana|IMT Kharkhoda]] in Sonipat district across 900 acres with an investment of ₹18,000 crores.{{Cite web|date=2021-11-14|title=Maruti Suzuki gets green signal to set up new plant at Sonepat|url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/delhi/maruti-suzuki-new-plant-sonepat-7621639/|access-date=2021-11-15|website=The Indian Express|language=en}} [[Haryana State Industrial and Infrastructure Development Corporation]] gives 900 acres of land to Maruti Suzuki for setting up a new plant in Industrial Model Township at [[Kharkhoda, Haryana]].{{Cite web|author=Manvir Saini|date=Nov 13, 2021|title=Haryana: 900 acres of land given to Maruti for the new plant in Sonipat's Kharkhoda district {{!}} Chandigarh News |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/chandigarh/haryana-900-acres-of-land-given-to-maruti-for-new-plant-in-sonipats-kharkhoda-district/articleshow/87688976.cms|access-date=2021-11-15|website=The Times of India|language=en}} In August 2022 [[Prime Minister of India]] [[Narendra Modi]] virtually laid the foundation stone of Maruti Suzuki's new manufacturing plant in [[Kharkhoda, Haryana|Kharkhoda]]. The operations will commence in 2028-29 taking the production capacity combined to 4.35 million units annually. ==Controversies== ===Industrial relations=== Since its founding in 1983, Maruti Udyog Limited has experienced problems with its labor force. The [[Labour in India|Indian labor]] it hired readily accepted Japanese work culture and the modern manufacturing process. In 1997, there was a change in ownership, and Maruti became predominantly government controlled. Shortly thereafter, conflict between the [[United Front (India, 1996)|United Front Government]] and Suzuki started. In 2000, a major industrial relations issue began and employees of Maruti went on an indefinite strike, demanding among other things, major revisions to their wages, incentives and pensions.{{cite book|title=Retail Management: Text And Cases|author=U.C. Mathur|year=2010|isbn=978-9380578668|pages=471–472|publisher=I. K. International Pvt }}{{cite news|title=Maruti staff to continue strike|publisher=The Hindu Business Line|date=28 September 2000|url=http://hindu.com/businessline/2000/09/28/stories/142807a6.htm|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140219115123/http://hindu.com/businessline/2000/09/28/stories/142807a6.htm|archive-date=19 February 2014}} Employees used [[slowdown]] in October 2000, to press a revision to their incentive-linked pay. In parallel, after elections and a new central government led by [[National Democratic Alliance (India)|NDA alliance]], India pursued a [[Disinvestment|disinvestment policy]]. Along with many other government owned companies, the new administration proposed to sell part of its stake in Maruti Suzuki in a public offering. The worker's union opposed this sell-off plan on the grounds that the company will lose a major business advantage of being subsidized by the Government, and the union has better protection while the company remains in control of the government.{{cite news|title=MUL union leaders on hunger strike|publisher=The Hindu Business Line|date=19 December 2000|url=http://www.hindu.com/businessline/2000/12/19/stories/141907a6.htm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130125111847/http://www.hindu.com/businessline/2000/12/19/stories/141907a6.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 January 2013}} The standoff between the [[Trade union|union]] and the management continued through 2001. The management refused union demands citing increased competition and lower margins. The central government privatized Maruti in 2002 and Suzuki became the majority owner of Maruti Udyog Limited.{{cite web|url=http://www.hartford-hwp.com/archives/52a/index-db.html|title=Article Timeline of Maruti Suzuki Labour Unrest, World History Archive|publisher=Hartford-hwp.com|access-date=10 October 2010}}{{cite news|title=Maruti disinvestment - Releasing the clutch|publisher=The Hindu Business Line|date=19 May 2002|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.in/iw/2002/05/19/stories/2002051900060700.htm}} ===Manesar violence=== On 18 July 2012, Maruti's [[Manesar]] plant was hit by violence. According to Maruti management, the production workers attacked supervisors and started a fire that killed company's General Manager of Human Resources Avineesh Dev and injured 100 other managers, including two Japanese [[expatriate]]s. Under the provisions of The Industrial Disputes Act for wages, the report claimed, employees are expected to be paid for the duration of the lockout.{{cite news|title=Maruti Suzuki declares lockout at Manesar factory|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/news-by-industry/auto/automobiles/maruti-suzuki-declares-lockout-at-manesar-factory/articleshow/15082063.cms|access-date=21 July 2012|newspaper=The Economic Times|date=22 July 2012|author=Chanchal Pal Chauhan}} On 26 July 2012, Maruti announced employees would not be paid for the period of lock-out in accordance with [[Indian labour laws|Indian labor laws]]. We will not compromise at all in such instances of barbaric, unprovoked violence." He also announced Maruti plans to continue manufacturing in Manesar, that [[Gujarat]] was an expansion opportunity and not an alternative to Manesar.{{cite news|title=Maruti to stay put at Manesar, planning new plant|date=21 July 2012|author=Chanchal Pal Chauhan|work=[[The Economic Times]]|url=http://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/news-by-industry/auto/automobiles/maruti-to-stay-put-at-manesar-planning-new-plant/articleshow/15064245.cms}}{{cite news|title=We will de-recognise Maruti Suzuki Workers' Union: Shinzo Nakanishi|author=Sharmistha Mukherjee & Surajeet Das Gupta|work=[[Business Standard]]|date=22 July 2012|url=http://business-standard.com/india/news/we-will-de-recognise-maruti-suzuki-workers-union-shinzo-nakanishi/481032/}} The company dismissed 500 workers accused of causing the violence and re-opened the plant on 21 August, saying it would produce 150 vehicles on the first day, less than 10% of its capacity. Analysts said that the shutdown was costing the company 1 billion rupees ($18 million) a day and costing the company market share.{{Cite news |url=http://www.timescolonist.com/business/Maruti+Suzuki+riot+plant+reopens+only+partial+capacity/7121376/story.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130204114233/http://www.timescolonist.com/business/Maruti+Suzuki+riot+plant+reopens+only+partial+capacity/7121376/story.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=4 February 2013 |title=Maruti Suzuki's riot-hit plant reopens but only at partial capacity |author=The Times Colonist |date=21 August 2012 |access-date=22 August 2012 |author-link=The Times Colonist }} In July 2013, the workers went on hunger strike to protest the continuing jailing of their colleagues and launched an online campaign to support their demands.{{Cite news |url=http://www.labourstartcampaigns.net/show_campaign.cgi?c=1889 |title=India: Free 147 jailed workers - support the hunger strikers |author= LabourStart |date=15 July 2013 |access-date=15 July 2013|author-link=LabourStart }} A total of 148 workers were charged with the murder of Human Resources Manager Avineesh Dev. The court dismissed charges against 117 of the workers. The remaining 13 workers were sentenced to life in imprisonment after being found guilty of the [[murder]] of General Manager of Human Resources Avineesh Dev. Twelve of the thirteen sentenced were office-bearers of the Maruti Suzuki Workers Union at the time of the alleged offences. Defense counsel [[Vrinda Grover]] stated, "We will file appeals against all convictions in the HC. The evidence, as it stands, cannot withstand legal scrutiny. Therefore, it is clear that this is targeted framing of these persons. We hope for justice in the superior court".{{Cite news|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/india/in-maruti-plant-violence-13-get-life-sentence-worker-unions-to-hold-rally-4575457/|title=In Maruti plant violence: 13 sentenced to life, worker unions to hold rally|last=Sakshi|first=Dayal|date=2017-03-19|work=Indian Express}} The Maruti Suzuki Workers Union is continuing to organize industrial action and protests calling for the workers to be released and criticizing the judgement and sentences an unjust.{{Cite web|url=https://marutisuzukiworkersunion.wordpress.com/2017/03/19/free-the-maruti-workers-13-maruti-union-members-given-life-sentence-for-struggling-for-union-formation-abolition-of-the-contract-worker-system/|title=Free the Maruti Workers! 13 Maruti Union members given 'Life Sentence' for Struggling for Union Formation &Abolition of the Contract Worker System|date=2017-03-19|website=Maruti Suzuki Workers Union}} An international appeal for the release of the workers has been made by the International Committee for the Fourth International (ICFI) and other organizations such as the People's Alliance for Democracy and Secularism (PADS).{{Cite web|url=http://www.wsws.org/en/articles/2017/03/20/pers-m20.html|title=Free the framed-up Maruti Suzuki workers!|date=2017-03-20|website=World Socialist Website}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.countercurrents.org/2017/03/19/demanding-justice-for-convicted-workers-of-maruti-suzuki/|title=Demanding Justice For Convicted Workers of Maruti Suzuki|last=Rao|first=Battini|website=Countercurrents.org|date=19 March 2017 }} ===Automotive safety=== Maruti Suzuki has been criticized for compromising safety in their products by automotive enthusiasts, journalists, and the [[Global NCAP]], as they are made lighter in terms of kerb weight to achieving higher fuel economy. Starting from January 2014, several of their made for India cars were crash tested at Global NCAP through the [[Global NCAP#Safer Cars for India|Safer Cars for India]] campaign, most of which have given disappointing results. Cars like [[Suzuki Alto|Alto]], [[Suzuki Swift|Swift]], [[Suzuki Celerio|Celerio]], [[Suzuki S-Presso|S-Presso]] (with driver's airbag), and [[Suzuki Eeco|Eeco]] which had no safety features like [[airbag]]s were awarded 0 stars, while [[Suzuki Wagon R|Wagon-R]] and [[Suzuki Swift|Swift]] (2018 model year) which had dual front airbags were awarded 2 stars out of 5. Only the [[Suzuki Vitara|Vitara]], [[suzuki Brezza|Brezza]] (4 stars) and [[Suzuki Ertiga|Ertiga]] (3 stars) have been awarded decent safety ratings.{{Cite web|url=https://www.globalncap.org/safercarsforindia|title=#SaferCarsForIndia|website=Globalncap.org|access-date=5 March 2022|archive-date=20 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220320025108/https://www.globalncap.org/safercarsforindia|url-status=dead}} Though Maruti Suzuki claimed that they were following the safety standards mandated by the Government of India, it however only implied with the safety features included in their cars and not the strong body shell or build quality which suffers the impact of the crash.{{Cite web|url=https://www.indiacarnews.com/news/crash-test-results-of-maruti-suzuki-cars-global-ncap-42873/|title=Crash Test Results of Maruti Suzuki Cars – Global NCAP|date=13 November 2020}} Maruti Suzuki has also come under fire for discrimination with customers in India, by making cars safe meant for exports to European and African markets.{{Cite web|url=https://news.abplive.com/news/auto/maruti-suzuki-s-presso-safer-in-africa-as-compared-to-india-reports-1400820|title=Maruti Suzuki S-Presso Safer In Africa As Compared To India: Reports|website=News.abplive.com|date=30 November 2020}} In November 2014, [[R. Maruti Suzuki India Limited is the Indian subsidiary of Japanese automaker Suzuki Motor Corporation. It is the largest automobile manufacturer in India, specializing in small cars. As of 2025, the company had a market capitalization of approximately US$50-55 billion. The company was established by the Government of India as Maruti Udyog Limited in February 1981 as a joint venture with Suzuki, the latter becoming the first Japanese automaker, as well as the first major foreign automaker, to invest in India.
Maruti opened its first production facility in Gurugram, Haryana, in 1982. Initially, Maruti was majority-owned by the Indian government, with Suzuki only taking a 26% stake during its establishment in 1982. The Indian government gradually reduced its stake, partially departed the business in 2003 by making it a public company and then sold all of its remaining shares to Suzuki Motor Corporation in 2007.
Maruti Suzuki has emerged as the largest Suzuki subsidiary in terms of production volume and sales. As of September 2022, the company had a leading market share of 42% in the Indian passenger car market.
